title: Gateway SDK primer & failover flows (working notes)
content:
Purpose
------
Working notes for a compact primer + quickstart that demonstrates SDK-level gateway helpers and recommended failover flows for production clients. Audience: SDK authors, solution eng, and backend engineers who embed Redwood calls into edge services. This is intentionally terse — we want a runnable path to a robust integration rather than a full PRD.

Why this doc exists (short):
- We still see users implement brittle direct-calls to /generate that break on transient infra spikes and on model substitutions.
- Provide small primitives in the SDK and an example CLI that show graceful fallback (lower-cost model, cached prefix, or queued retry) with telemetry hooks.
- Ship a one-file quickstart app that can be run in 10 minutes and shows how to integrate with Redwood Console metrics.

Top-level goals
-----------
- Demo resilient patterns: immediate fallback, client-side queueing, and degraded-mode outputs (shorter replies, embeddings-only).
- Offer 3 minimal SDK primitives: Circuit (health-aware routing), CacheLayer (prefix/KV), and PolicyEngine (fallback policy DSL).
- Provide a minimal CLI sample and a short local-test harness for SREs to reproduce timeouts and capacity fallbacks.

Audience assumptions
-------------------
- Engineers know REST and basic async programming but may not be infra experts.
- They want copy-paste examples and a diagnosed list of common failure modes.

Quickstart outline (10–15 minutes)
---------------------------------
1) Install: pip/npm package and get REDWOOD_API_KEY exported.
   - pip install redwood-gateway==0.3.0-preview
2) Run the example server locally: python gateway_quickstart.py --port 8080
3) Send a request: curl -X POST localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"summarize: quarterly notes"}'
4) Observe: service returns a response within 300ms using the primary model.
5) Simulate failure: toggle the quickstart flag --simulate-primary-outage and re-run the request.
6) Observe fallback path: system immediately routes to quantized variant or returns cached prefix + short completion.

Key SDK primitives (sketch)
---------------------------
- Circuit (health-aware routing):
  - tracks success / latency per model endpoint (sliding-window metrics)
  - exposes is_healthy(model_id) and record_result(model_id, success, latency)
  - built-in circuit-break thresholds tuned for token-latency spikes

- CacheLayer (prefix & KV):
  - transparent prefix caching for deterministic requests (conversation preamble, system message)
  - small LRU cache + Redis adapter for shared deployments
  - helper: should_fetch_from_cache(request_signature) => boolean

- PolicyEngine (fallback DSL):
  - simple YAML config with rules:
    - primary: redwood/gptx-8k
    - fallbacks: [redwood/gptx-8k-q4, redwood/gptx-4k, embeddings-only]
    - on_high_latency: trim_max_tokens: 64
    - on_5xx: immediate_fallback: true
  - runtime resolves policy to concrete action: retry-with-backoff, route-to-fallback, or return-degraded.

Recommended failover flows (practical)
-------------------------------------
1) Transient 5xx from primary: immediate small retry (100ms), then route-to-fallback-model (quantized). Emit metric: failover.count with tag reason=5xx
2) High token latency (p50>threshold): trim downstream tokens and route to fast model. Emit metric: latency-signal
3) Capacity-limited (429): queue request in short in-process ring-buffer (bounded, max 50ms queuing) and signal on_trace to Redwood Console; if queue full, return degrade response with reason: overloaded
4) Cold-started serving region: route to cross-region variant while honoring customer data region constraints (configurable in PolicyEngine)

Degraded-mode examples (user-visible)
------------------------------------
- Short reply: "short-summary" variant (<=64 tokens) with explicit header that says "degraded: true".
- Embedding fallback: if generation fails, return a best-effort embedding + search-based snippet and label source="embedding-fallback"

CLI sample commands to show behavior
----------------------------------
- Start: python gateway_quickstart.py --mode normal
- Force 5xx: python gateway_quickstart.py --mode fail-primary-5xx
- Show metrics snapshot: curl localhost:8080/metrics | jq .failover

Observability & telemetry requirements (minimum)
------------------------------------------------
- Emit: model_id, latency_ms, tokens_out, result_code, failover_reason, policy_decision
- Link traces to Redwood Console via trace_id header and include request_signature in logs for debugging
- Expose a small /debug endpoint that returns the decision tree for a recent request (redacted)

Acceptance checklist (for developer-experience owner)
---------------------------------------------------
- [ ] 1-file quickstart that runs locally with zero infra.
- [ ] Unit tests for Circuit and CacheLayer (edge cases: cache stampede, negative caching).
- [ ] Demo script that reproduces each failover path deterministically.
- [ ] Short README + 3 screenshots of Console: failover metrics, rollout trace, and policy change timeline.
- [ ] PR with README and example merged and a follow-up RFC for production hardening.

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes)
--------------------------------
- Do we return degraded outputs by default or require opt-in? (privacy/regulatory implications for some customers)
- How opinionated should PolicyEngine be (DSL vs composable primitives)? Start minimal — YAML rules.
- Cache invalidation semantics when a model version is rolled out: conservative TTLs + model-version keying.
- Multi-tenant telemetry costs: keep sample rates configurable per org

Next steps (short)
-----------------
- Draft the one-file quickstart and get internal review from solutions-eng (DEVEX-718 assigned).
- Wire basic metrics into Console (trace_id mapping) and demo to SRE in next office hours.
- Drive a small user study with two internal teams integrating the quickstart into their microservices and collect failure stories.

Notes to self (todo + timeline)
-----------------------------
- Prototype Circuit + CacheLayer (2 days)
- Write quickstart and three deterministic failure modes (3 days)
- Internal review + minor UX polish (2 days)
- Ship preview package and gather feedback (1 week)

References and links (for reader)
--------------------------------
- Confluence brief: /pages/CON-3421-gateway-sdk-overview (design notes)
- Related jira: DEVEX-718 (gateway primitives epic)
- Example PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/842

Random shorthand / scraps (keep)
-----------------------------
- "degrade fast, fail safe" is the motto for the quickstart.
- Keep the example code to ~120 LOC; no framework heavy deps.
- Emphasize testability: deterministic seeds for the mocked model server.

End.
